operator: `operator` only for what the operator alone can decide: a choice they reserved, requirements of theirs that contradict each other, or words of theirs that read more than one way where the reading changes the result.

summary.description: One sentence the operator reads, in the language they wrote in: what this turn achieved, found or is stuck on. No "I", no Argus file names such as CHECKPOINT.md, no protocol words; plain text, no Markdown.

note.description: For whoever holds the work next: what changed, the decisive check, what is still missing, and why it goes to them. The operator does not see it.

ask.description: With to=operator only: one question in the operator's language, with two to five answers to pick from, or none for an open question.

assumptions.description: Each place where the operator's words read more than one way, the reading changes the result, and you chose one without asking: the reading you chose and the one you did not. [] when there is none. The operator is shown each one with the result. Unsure whether it is theirs to decide? Ask with to=operator.

engineer.description: Hand the work on when your turn is over; the call ends your turn, so do not repeat it in your reply. to: reviewer, the work is ready for the independent review (do not start one yourself or through a subagent); done, the milestone is complete and the task requires no independent review; engineer, you keep working next turn; planner, the task is mis-scoped; manager, the process is stuck (an environment, tool, access, credential or quota failure, or the same error repeating) and needs the Manager to debug it; operator, a decision only the operator can make.

review.description: Submit your judgment of this candidate; the call ends your turn. to: done accepts it, only after you checked each requirement and symptom the task (this increment) states, and each acceptance criterion, against the deliverable: tests the Engineer wrote show the code matches its reading of the task, not that the reading is right, and a stated symptom called intended or out of scope needs support in the task text itself; engineer returns concrete in-scope repairs, named in note; planner, the task or plan is wrong; manager, the process is stuck (an environment, tool or access failure you cannot judge past) and needs the Manager to debug it; requirements of the operator's that conflict are the operator's to settle; operator, a decision only the operator can make.

learning.description: With to=done: is anything from this task worth keeping for later work: a failure, a correction, a surprise, a new technique, a reusable pattern, a recalled lesson this task's evidence disproved? When unsure, worth_reflecting.

session_signal.description: An observed role-session quality problem, not an ordinary task repair.

unverifiable.description: Not with to=done: a decisive check that cannot happen here, and the risk left. Where the operator can be asked, leaving it unverified is their decision: ask them with to=operator and accept_risk. Where they cannot, the Manager sees this and decides whether to accept that risk.

impossible_because.description: Required when you call a check impossible here because what it needs exists only at grading or deploy time: the task, packet or environment statement that says so, quoted verbatim, and its source ('task', or a workspace file the packet names or unchanged since work on this objective began; never one written or edited since). The host checks the quote. Without such a statement the check is missing, not impossible.

residual_risk.description: Only with to=done, when one decisive check stays unverified because it is impossible here and leaving it so was accepted: by the operator choosing to accept it on the question you raised with accept_risk, or, in a run with no operator, by the Manager (cite the risk id listed under Accepted residual risk). Name the check exactly as accepted. Without that acceptance, do not accept the candidate. The evidence you judged it from must be something you read yourself. A test fixture counts only if it follows the documented interface or schema, runs the real entry point (not a stub of the code under test) and is labelled a test fixture. The Engineer's word alone is never that evidence.

acceptance.description: The Manager's risk id, or the operator's decision id; the host checks the recorded choice, not this text.

accept_risk.description: With to=operator, when the question is whether to leave one check impossible here unverified: name the check and the risk. The host offers the choice to accept that risk or keep the check, in place of ask's options; only choosing it accepts.

plan.description: Hand on your plan; the call ends your turn. to: engineer, the tasks below start, or with none the work in flight decides what comes next (invent no work that needs results still in flight); manager, the process is stuck for a mechanical reason no plan can route around (a failure that keeps repeating, an environment, tool, credential or quota failure, a loop of hand-offs), and the Manager debugs it; operator, only the operator can unblock it (what they want, or no route left that fits it); while your question to them is unanswered, hand to=operator with it again: it stays as first asked and nothing new reaches them; done, the operator's complete goal is met, with no tasks. The stage moves when the completion gate finds the evidence ready: propose it with the task that closes the stage, or with advance_to_stage; you never declare it moved or the project done yourself. You are called again when something new arrives: a mission ends, the operator writes, the Manager directs. summary: the decision and the next step as a colleague would say it, without field names, status words, routine steps or Argus's own bookkeeping, and nothing the last summary said.

tasks.description: The work to start: each task's decision, inputs and check, not who does or reviews it.

objective.description: The full, actionable description the Engineer works from.

key.description: This task's name for deps in this call.

deps.description: Keys of tasks in this call that must finish first.

waypoint_id.description: The id of the operator's required step (必经步骤) this task fulfils; at most one.

scope.description: final_submission only for the final independent certification task.

parallel_safe.description: Co-runs with other parallel_safe tasks; needs owns_paths. Stage-closing and framework-maintenance work runs alone.

owns_paths.description: The literal, relative paths only this task writes, no wildcards, disjoint from the others'.

stage_package.description: A reviewed interim package for the operator while the work goes on.

gpu_count.description: GPUs the task holds while it runs.

cpu_count.description: CPU cores the task keeps busy.

vertical.description: The mission's role, when it differs from the campaign's.

retire.description: Pending work that is refuted, closed or a renamed repeat; never running or done work.

settle_instructions.description: Each OperatorContext entry tagged `revision N` that this decision carries out, rules out, or (for a subagent report) has already taken into account.

advance_to_stage.description: The stage this plan moves to; left out, the stage holds.

plan_update.description: The full new RESEARCH_PLAN.md, when the direction changed; left out, it stays.

about_waypoint.description: With to=operator: the id of the operator's required step your question doubts (offer keep / change / remove).

manager.description: Call it only when Argus must act on this turn; otherwise just answer. While the team is working, call it on every turn: to=manager with nothing else when the message changes nothing for the team. to: team hands the work to the team as a ticket (goal, acceptance, constraints, context); operator asks the operator what only they can decide (the operator sees your ask, its question and options, instead of your reply, so the question carries what they need to decide); manager keeps the turn yours while Argus applies the settings, control, grants or lasting rules you file. Your reply still goes to the operator.

goal.description: With to=team: the outcome the team delivers, standalone, in the operator's language.

acceptance.description: With to=team: the checks that prove the goal is met.

constraints.description: With to=team: limits the operator stated, verbatim; never invented.

context.description: With to=team: paths of the files the team should read first.

path.description: The plan file, by its workspace-relative path.

summary.description: The plan in a few to a dozen lines, in the operator's language: what the operator confirms before work starts.

plan.description: With to=team, when you wrote a plan file: where it is and its summary. The operator sees them on the ticket before work starts.

lifetime.description: With to=team, or a steer: standing for ongoing intent and when the operator wants Argus to carry on by itself without waiting for them (it turns continuous mode on), else bounded.

vertical.description: With to=team: the team's workflow, from the menu in the team-handoff rules, or a project domain's slug; a new reusable slug only when none fits.

domain.description: With vertical=research: an optional research domain from the menu.

workflow_mode.description: With to=team: direct for one coherent Engineer task, staged for dependent phases.

start_stage.description: With workflow_mode=direct: the stage it starts at, if not the first.

workflow_profile.description: With to=team, for a vertical that offers workflow profiles: the profile from its menu.

workflow_stages.description: With workflow_profile=custom: the stages to compose, in order.

research_direction_mode.description: With vertical=research: broad while the direction is open, locked for the operator's concrete idea.

target_venue.description: With vertical=research: only a venue the operator named.

require_independent_review.description: With to=team: false only when the operator waived independent review.

operator_decides_stages.description: With to=team: true only when the operator said they want to decide stage moves themselves; the team then asks them before a stage moves.

waypoint_id.description: With to=team, when the ticket carries out one of the operator's required steps (必经步骤): that step's id; the ticket then does that step only. Leave it out for other work.

intake.description: A lasting rule the operator gave: standing_directive to govern later turns (`以后都用中文`), with preference_value the rule only; otherwise preference, credential_grant or revocation; objective_amendment when it edits the live mission. roles: the roles it applies to, [] for all.

config.description: Settings the operator explicitly changes, one entry per setting. model and effort take roles ([] for all); the other settings take none. Questions and task-local wishes change no setting.

control.description: Only for an explicit command: pause stops the campaign; abort ends the current mission; steer gives the running mission a new direction, priority, method or constraint, in directive; with no mission running, a new or changed goal is a to=team ticket instead. quote: the operator's own words giving the command, verbatim.

authorization.description: Grants the operator explicitly gives; questions and quotes grant nothing.

operator_question_policy.description: forbid only for an explicit command against questions; allow only when they are explicitly re-enabled.

name.description: A new topic for this conversation, in the operator's language; left out while the topic holds.

answer.description: With to=manager, when the message answers a question a paused task waits on (listed with the message): item, that task's id; option, the id of the offered answer it picks, if it picks one; decision, the explicit instruction for the Planner and Engineer the answer gives, naming any earlier constraint it supersedes. Leave it out when the message does not answer it, or not enough to go on; then ask back in your reply.

workflow_setup.description: Only while you set up a reusable workflow with the operator (the workflow-setup rules), with to=manager: prepare, once its scope is agreed, with name, purpose, brief, title and summary; skip to handle the request directly instead; cancel to drop the setup. A question about it goes to=operator with ask; a plain answer needs no call.

purpose.description: Its capability scope, for matching future tasks.

brief.description: Its reusable definition: scope and exclusions, parameterized inputs and missing-data handling, outputs, method and reference plan, limitations and validation cases. No personal facts, one-off answers or project paths.

title.description: The agreed task's short name, as the operator reads it.

summary.description: The agreed task in two to four sentences: the deliverable, its essential inputs and limits.

supervise.description: Record your judgment of the team's course; the call ends your turn. When work climbed to you because the process is stuck, you debug the process, not the work: note gives your diagnosis (the cause and what you fixed); to=team retries it with the holder, to=planner gives the Planner your diagnosis to replan around, to=operator asks only what needs them (credentials, money, scope, an irreversible step); what the operator wants, the plan, accepting a candidate and the stage stay with their owners. to: team, the course is right, and with a note your corrected instruction, read by whoever holds the work at their next boundary; planner, your note needs new planning (tasks to add, retire or replace); operator, work handed to you waits on a choice only the operator can make, and the task waits on their answer; stop parks this mission, when changing direction will not help. summary: the decisive observed condition and what happens next, naming no task ids.

evidence_refs.description: The evidence_refs paths your decision rests on.

consultation.description: The advisor consultation your decision used, and whether you adopted its result.

risk.description: Only when the operator cannot be asked: accept the residual risk of one check a Reviewer showed impossible here, when the Reviewer read the best evidence reachable here; or revoke an acceptance that no longer holds. A test fixture counts only if it follows the documented interface or schema, runs the real entry point (not a stub of the code under test) and is labelled a test fixture.

observe.description: Your look at how the team's work flows; the call ends the look. Leave remark out when the flow is fine.

remark.description: When the flow is off: one sentence for the Manager, in the operator's language, saying what you saw and why it matters. Plain words: no file names, event types or timestamps; where you saw it goes in seen_at.

seen_at.description: With remark: the ts of the events.jsonl lines it rests on.

reflect.description: What your reflection leaves for the host; the call ends your turn. The pages you wrote are read from disk.

retire.description: Saved pages this task showed wrong for the current facts, or whose problem has since been fixed: the host takes each out of the library and records why. [] when there is none.

reviewed_fact.description: Only when asked to judge a Reviewer-confirmed result for the reviewed-facts digest: keep it or not; to keep it, the fact and the refs it rests on, copied from the allowed refs.

consolidate.description: The vertical's principles.md, as fields; the host writes the file from them.

description.description: One sentence saying what the principles cover.

principles.description: The working rules the listed lessons teach, merged where they say the same thing; [] when they share none yet. Keep a current principle only while two listed lessons still support it.

rule.description: One plain imperative sentence a colleague could follow.

evidence.description: The lesson pages that support it, as their listed paths (pages/lessons/<file>.md).

retire.description: Listed lessons a later one shows wrong, or whose problem has since been fixed: they support nothing, and the host retires them. [] when there is none.
